name: Saguaro Cactus
intro: A saguaro is a very tall cactus. It lives in the hot, dry desert.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A saguaro is a giant green cactus.
It can grow taller than a house.
Many saguaros have arms that point up.
Sharp spines cover the cactus.
A waxy skin helps keep water inside.

sections.title: Where does it grow?
sentences: Saguaros grow only in the Sonoran Desert.
Most of them grow in southern Arizona.
Some grow in Mexico too.
In cooler places, they grow on warm, sunny hillsides.

sections.title: What does it need?
sentences: A saguaro needs rain to grow.
Its roots spread wide just under the ground.
The roots soak up rain fast.
The stem stores water and gets fatter.
A baby saguaro needs shade from a nurse tree.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A saguaro starts as a tiny black seed.
It grows very, very slowly.
After 10 years, it may be only about 1 inch tall.
It gets its first flowers at about 35 years old.
Many saguaros live more than 150 years.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Saguaro flowers are white and open at night.
Bats drink nectar from the flowers.
The saguaro flower is the state wildflower of Arizona.
Woodpeckers make nest holes in the cactus.
Each red fruit holds about 2,000 tiny seeds.

vocab.meaning: A plant with a thick stem that stores water.
A dry place that gets very little rain.
Sharp, pointy parts that protect a cactus.
A tree that shades a baby plant growing under it.
